title: CRLR/82/2014 of Karan Sethi Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 82 of 2014
Karan Sethi ....... Revisionist
 versus
State of Uttarakhand ......... Respondent
Mr. B. M. Pingal, Advocate present for the revisionist.
Mr. V. S. Pal, AGA present for the State.
U.C. Dhyani, J.(Oral)

The present criminal revision is filed by the
revisionist through his natural guardian and mother, being
aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 04.04.2014
whereby the criminal appeal preferred by the juvenile in
conflict with law (for short 'juvenile') was dismissed, vide
order dated 04.04.2014. When the juvenile moved an
application for bail in connection with F.I.R No. 34/2014
under Section 302 IPC, P.S, Gadarpur. His bail application
was dismissed by the Principal Magistrate, Juvenile Justice
Board, Udham Singh Nagar on 24.03.2014.
Aggrieved against the said order, a criminal appeal
was preferred by the juvenile. The same was dismissed and
the order passed by the Juvenile Justice Board on
24.03.2014 was affirmed. The FIR was lodged by the father
of the deceased against four named accused persons,
including the revisionist, on 17.3.2014 at P.S. Gadarpur for
the offence punishable under Section 302 IPC.
It was alleged that the victim was killed by the
accused persons with a broken bottle. The victim was
thrown in a canal. When the witnesses took the victim to

2
the Government Hospital, Gadarpur, but he could not
survive. The victim was playing near Shiv Rice Mill when
the incident took place. The revisionist was arrested on
19.3.2014 and, since then, he is in observation home. One
of the grounds taken up by the revisionist in the revision is
that co-accused Goldi and Vicky were given in the
supurdgi of their parents on 19.3.2014. A clarification was
sought from learned A.G.A in this respect. Learned A.G.A.
obtained a report from the Investigating Officer, who
submitted the report that whereas Mukesh Rawat and
present revisionist were arrested, the other co-accused
Goldi and Vicky were not arrested in as much as, the
evidence was being collected against them. In the FIR, the
names of all four accused were mentioned in the FIR.
Same role was assigned to all the four accused. Then, how
a different treatment could be meted out to two of them?
Witness Bhoop Singh has stated in his statement under
Section 161 Cr.P.C. that all the four accused, namely,
Mukesh, Karan, Vicky and Goldi were present at the place
of incident. Mukesh and Karan Sethi (present revisionist)
lifted his brother (victim) and took him to hospital. There
is no evidence on record to suggest that the case of Mukesh
Rawat was distinguishable from the case of Goldi and
Vicky, who were given in supurdgi of their parents.
Learned lower appellate Court has also stated in the
impugned order dated 04.04.2014 that the revisionist is a
regular student of Class-XI in Spring Dell Public School,
Kathgodam. According to the report given by District
Probation Officer, revisionist's father is a Village
Panchayat Development Officer and his mother is a

3
Principal in ANM Training Institute. The District
Probation Officer has given good report regarding the
conduct of the revisionist. It appears that the revisionist
committed such crime on account of his association with
bad elements.
In such a situation, this Court is of the opinion that no
different treatment can be given to the present revisionist
than the treatment given to co-accused Goldi and Vicky
with similar role. The criminal revision is, therefore,
allowed. The impugned orders dated 04.04.2014 and
24.03.2014 are set aside. As a consequence thereof, his
bail application is also allowed. Let the revisionist be
enlarged on bail on his parents' executing personal bonds
and furnishing two sureties, each of the like amount to the
satisfaction of the Juvenile Justice Board, Udham Singh
Nagar.
